newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-MOIN SPARKLES AS PAKISTAN BUILD LEAD OF 102.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MOIN SPARKLES AS PAKISTAN BUILD LEAD OF 102.

text.p: Wicketkeeper Moin Khan hit a sparkling half-century to put Pakistan ahead by 102 runs against Zimbabwe at lunch on the second day of the second and final test on Friday.
Moin hit an unbeaten 58, his third half-century in 21 tests, and checked the Zimbabwe bowlers who took four wickets in the morning session.

Starting the day at 114 for three in reply to Zimbabwe's modest first innings of 133, Pakistan lost Saeed Anwar (81), Hasan Raza (27), Wasim Akram (35) and Mohammad Hussain (0). At lunch Pakistan were 235 for seven.
Anwar, 69 overnight, smashed three more boundaries before he chased a wide delivery from paceman Everton Matambanadzo and edged an easy catch to Andy Flower behind the stumps.

His partner Raza, the youngest player to appear in a test match at the age of 14 years and 227 days, added seven runs to his overnight 20 before he edged a catch to David Houghton at first slip off leg-spinner Paul Strang.
Akram and Moin then added a rapid 53 for the sixth wicket before Mpumilo Mbangwn bowled the Pakistani captain as he aimed a big drive.
Akram, who made an unbeaten 257 in the drawn first test at Sheikhupura, scored fluently and his innings contained seven fours from 47 balls.
Debutant Mohammad Hussain was next to go at 200 when he was run out.
Moin reached his half-century with a streaky shot off Strang, his 50 including 10 fours from 74 balls.
